content.comment_body: Hello, I have a question about how AWS handles communication intervals. I've configured my [product_name] to send an update every 10 minutes to AWS, and that part is working fine. However, when I subscribe to the MQTT topic '/get/accepted', my [product_name] starts sending messages every second. Is this normal behavior? It seems unusual to me. Best regards, [user_name]

Hi! Honestly, using AWS with [product_name] version [version_no] tends to be complicated. I suggest considering [product_name] version [version_no], which includes improved options for cloud connections, such as with Azure. Calculating the cost of data exchange with AWS can be tricky and unpredictable! A solution I implemented involved [product_name] version [version_no] working with a Raspberry Pi using Node-Red, and connecting through Taggo I/O cloud via MQTT protocol. Taggo I/O is a user-friendly tool in my experience.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are uncertain about the unexpectedly high frequency of MQTT messages sent from their [product_name] device to AWS when monitoring specific topics. The implementation currently leads to much more frequent updates than anticipated, and this behavior isn't clearly explained in existing documentation. This causes confusion and concerns about unnecessary data transmission and the impact on cloud service costs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the message frequency on subscribed topics to follow the configured 10-minute update interval instead of sending data every second, seeking more consistent and manageable communication rates.
